title: Verifiable compliance archives and templated reporting for tenant-scoped exports
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a tenant-aware, auditable export service that produces signed, templated compliance reports (PDF and CSV) and a live dashboard snapshot. Targets: tenant-scoped evidence bundles, per-tenant residency filters, retention-aware inclusion rules, and scheduled delivery with verifiable integrity metadata. This work unblocks enterprise customers who require periodic forensic snapshots and machine-readable ledger exports for audits and regulatory reviews.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/exports triggers a tenant-scoped export job with residency and retention parameters and returns a job id
Output formats: system generates both a human-facing PDF (templated with metadata and signatures) and machine-facing CSV (normalized event ledger) for each completed job
Integrity: each exported artifact includes a verifiable SHA256 hash and a signed manifest (KMS-backed) stored alongside the export
Delivery: scheduled exports can be configured per-tenant to deliver to S3 (regional buckets), SFTP endpoints, or via encrypted email attachments, respecting tenant residency settings
Retention-awareness: exported data respects tenant retention policies and omits records past retention windows or logs omissions in the manifest
Dashboard: Console shows export job history, status, delivery attempts, and per-file integrity hashes; tenants can re-download artifacts for 90 days by default
Access control: only tenant admins and authorized org roles can create, view, or download exports; actions are recorded in audit logs
Performance: medium-sized export (30 days, 10M events) completes within SLA window configurable per plan (default 4 hours)
Observability: traces and metric hooks available (job duration, bytes exported, failure rate) and surfaced in Redwood Console
Security review: external-facing delivery channels and KMS signing flow pass security review checklist
implementation_notes: Backend: new export microservice 'evidence-curator' that composes, signs, and stages artifacts. Prefer batch streaming to avoid memory spikes.
KMS: use customer-managed keys where available; fallback to Redwood-managed KMS with audit trail. Sign manifests with KMS asymmetric keys to allow external verification.
Residency: export job planner must query tenant residency rules and select target region S3 bucket or neutral staging in the tenant's allowed region.
Retention: exporter consults retention index to include/exclude events; exclusions must be logged with reason codes in manifest
Formats: PDF engine using templating layer (liquid-style templates) and CSV with strict column schema versioning (v1 initially)
Delivery: implement modular sinks (S3, SFTP, HTTP webhook) with retry/backoff, idempotency keys, and delivery receipts stored as events
Observability: emit events to trace span per job, expose Prometheus metrics and job-level logs to central ELK with tenant tagging
Scale: implement chunked export + parallel workers for large job windows; use cursored reads from evidence store to avoid full table scans
Data model: exported manifest includes fields: job_id, tenant_id, residency_region, retention_cutoff, included_record_count, omitted_count, sha256_list, signed_manifest_url
Backward compatibility: console API must fallback to older ad-hoc CSV export for small non-templated requests until rollout complete
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): internal tenants + 3 enterprise beta customers, feature-flagged; manual SFTP and S3 delivery only
Phase 2 (beta): add PDF templating, KMS signing, and console UX for job scheduling; expand to customer-managed KMS
Phase 3 (GA): add webhook delivery, SLA tiers, and retention-aware omission reporting; enable self-serve scheduling in Console
Canary policy: start with single region (us-west-2) and limit concurrent export jobs per tenant to 2 during rollout
Fallbacks: on large failures, auto-fallback to compressed CSV-only export and notify tenant admin via console and email
qa_checks: End-to-end export verification with seeded data including retention edge-cases
Signature validation test: externally verify signed manifest using public key
Delivery resilience: simulate SFTP/S3 outages and validate retries and receipts
Residency enforcement: try cross-region delivery and assert rejection when tenant policy disallows
Performance tests: synthetic 10M-event export with target completion under SLA in staging
Authorization tests: ensure RBAC prevents cross-tenant downloads
Schema compatibility: verify CSV v1 against parser used by downstream compliance tools
risks: Large exports could overwhelm IO and increase platform costs if not chunked and throttled
Signing keys mismanagement could prevent verification by customers; require strict KMS rotation/backup
Residency misconfigurations could cause cross-border data transfers; need strong validation and tests
Delivery endpoints provided by customers (SFTP) may be unreliable and require advanced retry/backoff
PDF templating must avoid PII leakage in headers/metadata; template sandboxing required
open_questions: Should manifests be signed with a per-tenant key or a platform-wide key by default?
Do we support multi-file exports (chunked artifacts) with a top-level index file in GA or wait for beta?
What is the canonical retention reporting format for regulators (include omitted counts or show sampled records)?
Do we surface a permanent download link after export or rotate temporary signed URLs?
